_meta.purpose: Deterministic ingredient -> allergen/diet-exclusion lookup used before any LLM call. This is the safety net: allergen decisions come from this table, not from a model guess.
_meta.allergen_categories: FDA 'Big 9' core (milk, egg, fish, crustacean_shellfish, tree_nut, peanut, wheat, soybean, sesame; coconut excluded from tree_nut per FDA's Jan 2025 guidance) PLUS molluscs, mustard, celery -- added after cross-checking Open Food Facts' allergens taxonomy (static.openfoodfacts.org/data/taxonomies/allergens.json, EU-style ~27 category list) and finding at least one ingredient actually used in this dataset for each. Molluscs matters most for Thai food (squid, mussels, oyster sauce are common) and isn't in the FDA-9. OFF's taxonomy also has sulphites and lupin categories, not added here because no ingredient in this dataset currently maps to them -- add them when a relevant ingredient (e.g. dried fruit/wine for sulphites) shows up. See DATA_SOURCES.md.
_meta.off_taxonomy_caveat: Open Food Facts' allergens.json includes Thai-language names per category, but they are community-contributed and not all reliable -- e.g. its Thai translation for 'en:nuts' is the word for 'almond' specifically, not a general term for nuts. Treat OFF's translations as a lead to verify, not a fact to copy -- do not surface them to end users unverified.
_meta.authorship: Hand-built starting map, cross-referenced against OFF's allergen taxonomy for category completeness. Ingredient-level entries are still developer-authored, not pulled from a verified ingredient database (OFF's live API is barcode/product-oriented, not free-text NLP -- see DATA_SOURCES.md). MUST be reviewed and expanded by someone with Thai food knowledge before being trusted for real allergy-safety decisions.
_meta.diet_exclusion_logic: vegan excludes any animal product (meat, fish, shellfish, molluscs, egg, dairy); vegetarian (lacto-ovo) excludes meat/fish/shellfish/molluscs but allows egg/dairy; pescatarian excludes meat but allows fish/shellfish/molluscs/egg/dairy

curry paste.note: many traditional Thai curry pastes include shrimp paste, but not all recipes -- verify per dish

massaman curry paste.note: recipes vary; some massaman pastes omit shrimp paste -- verify per dish

soy sauce.note: traditionally brewed with wheat, but gluten-free/tamari versions exist -- verify per product

coconut milk.note: coconut removed from FDA tree_nut allergen category in Jan 2025 guidance; track as its own allergy category if needed, not tree_nut

pickled mustard greens.note: a brassica vegetable (mustard plant leaves), not the mustard seed/condiment -- not treated as the 'mustard' allergen

msg.note: monosodium glutamate is not classified as a major allergen by FDA or EU; some people report sensitivity but it is not an allergen category tracked here
